questions.stem: Which city hosted the inaugural Summer Olympic Games of the modern era in 1896?

options.option_text: Paris, France (host city of the 1900 Summer Olympics)
Athens, Greece (host city of the 1896 inaugural Olympics)
London, England (host city of the 1908 Summer Olympics)
Stockholm, Sweden (host city of the 1912 Summer Olympics)

questions.explanation: Athens, Greece hosted the first modern Olympics in 1896, selected to honour the ancient Greek origins of the Games. Paris is a common wrong choice because Pierre de Coubertin was French and Paris hosted the very next Games in 1900, but the inaugural edition was awarded to Athens.

questions.stem: The tradition of the Olympic torch relay — where the flame is lit at Olympia, Greece, and carried overland to the host city — was first introduced at which Games?

options.option_text: 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, when the cauldron flame debuted in the stadium
1936 Berlin Olympics, organised under the Nazi German administration
1948 London Olympics, revived as a symbol after the World War II hiatus
1952 Helsinki Olympics, introduced to mark post-war international unity

questions.explanation: The relay from Olympia to the host city was introduced in 1936 Berlin, devised by Carl Diem. A common confusion: the 1928 Amsterdam Games introduced a flame burning inside the stadium cauldron, but that is distinct from the torch relay starting in Olympia, which is a 1936 innovation.

questions.stem: The Olympic flag with five interlocking coloured rings was first officially unfurled at which Olympic Games?

options.option_text: 1912 Stockholm Olympics, the year the rings design was first unveiled publicly
1920 Antwerp Olympics, the first Games held after World War I ended
1924 Paris Olympics, chosen to coincide with the Olympic centenary year
1928 Amsterdam Olympics, also the debut of the stadium Olympic flame cauldron

questions.explanation: Though Pierre de Coubertin designed the five-ring symbol in 1913 and it was publicly presented in 1914, the flag was first flown at the 1920 Antwerp Games. Option A is a trap because the rings were designed/revealed around 1913–14, not first flown then. Option D is wrong because the 1928 cauldron was a separate, later innovation.

questions.stem: Which Indian athlete became the first woman from India to win Olympic medals at two different Olympic Games?

options.option_text: Saina Nehwal, badminton bronze medallist at the 2012 London Olympics
Mary Kom, boxing bronze medallist at the 2012 London Olympics
P.V. Sindhu, silver at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020 Olympics
Karnam Malleswari, weightlifting bronze medallist at Sydney 2000 Olympics

questions.explanation: P.V. Sindhu won silver in badminton at Rio 2016 and bronze at Tokyo 2020, becoming the first Indian woman to medal at two separate Olympics. Saina Nehwal and Mary Kom each won a single Olympic medal (2012). Karnam Malleswari was the first Indian woman to win any Olympic medal (2000) but earned only one.

questions.stem: The ancient Greek concept of 'Ekecheiria', observed during the ancient Olympic Games and symbolically revived by the IOC, refers to which practice?

options.option_text: Lighting the sacred flame at the Temple of Hera in ancient Olympia
A sacred truce suspending armed conflicts for the duration of the Games
The ceremonial procession of athletes representing all Greek city-states
Dedicating athletic victories as religious offerings to Zeus at Olympia

questions.explanation: Ekecheiria literally means 'holding of hands' and refers to the Olympic Truce, where warring Greek city-states suspended hostilities during the Games. The IOC revived this symbolically in 1992. Option A describes the torch-lighting ceremony, which is a separate modern adaptation of ancient ritual, not Ekecheiria.

questions.stem: India's unbroken run of Olympic gold medals in field hockey spanned six consecutive Games. Which pair of years correctly brackets this historic streak?

options.option_text: 1924 to 1952, with India's first Olympic gold won at the Paris Games
1928 to 1956, with the 1940 and 1944 Games cancelled due to World War II
1928 to 1964, as India won gold in Tokyo without any gap in between
1932 to 1956, since India won silver and not gold at the 1928 Amsterdam Games

questions.explanation: India won gold in 1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, and 1956 — six consecutive Games. The 1940 and 1944 Games were cancelled due to WWII and do not break the streak. Option C is wrong because India won silver in 1960 Rome (Pakistan took gold), so there IS a gap before the 1964 Tokyo gold. Option D is wrong because India did win gold at the 1928 Amsterdam Games.

questions.stem: In 2021, the International Olympic Committee modified the Olympic motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' by adding a fourth Latin word. Which word was added and what does it mean?

options.option_text: 'Sanius' meaning Healthier, added to reflect post-pandemic athlete welfare
'Communiter' meaning Together, added to reflect the collective global spirit
'Aequius' meaning Fairer, added to reinforce the IOC's gender equity pledge
'Audacius' meaning Bolder, added to inspire athletes to push past old limits

questions.explanation: 'Communiter' (Together) was added at the IOC Session in Tokyo in July 2021, making the full motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius – Communiter'. It was proposed to emphasise solidarity in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. The other options are plausible-sounding Latin fabrications and were never officially proposed — this exact word and meaning is frequently tested in recent GK rounds.
